claim: Antibody binding to cell surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity.
source: Antibody binding to cell surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity, and the location of an epitope can altogether determine the immunological outcome of a host-target interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about antibody-cell surface protein interactions.

claim: The location of an epitope can determine the immunological outcome of a host-target interaction.
source: Antibody binding to cell surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity, and the location of an epitope can altogether determine the immunological outcome of a host-target interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Techniques available today for epitope identification are costly, time-consuming, and unsuited for high-throughput analysis.
source: Techniques available today for epitope identification are costly, time-consuming, and unsuited for high-throughput analysis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a characterization of current methods.

claim: Cellular morphology typically varies.
source: Cellular morphology typically varies, and antibodies often bind heterogeneously across a cell surface, making traditional particle-averaging strategies challenging for accurate native antibody localization.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of cellular systems.

claim: Antibodies often bind heterogeneously across a cell surface.
source: Cellular morphology typically varies, and antibodies often bind heterogeneously across a cell surface, making traditional particle-averaging strategies challenging for accurate native antibody localization.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of antibody binding.

claim: Traditional particle-averaging strategies are challenging for accurate native antibody localization due to variable cellular morphology and heterogeneous antibody binding.
source: Cellular morphology typically varies, and antibodies often bind heterogeneously across a cell surface, making traditional particle-averaging strategies challenging for accurate native antibody localization.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods based on known characteristics of cells and antibody binding.

claim: The authors have developed a method called SiteLoc for imaging-based molecular localization on cellular surface proteins.
source: In the present work, we have developed a method, SiteLoc, for imaging-based molecular localization on cellular surface proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary contribution of the work.

claim: Nanometer-scale resolution is achieved through localization in one dimension, namely, the distance from a bound ligand to a reference surface.
source: Nanometer-scale resolution is achieved through localization in one dimension, namely, the distance from a bound ligand to a reference surface.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the method's approach.

claim: The SiteLoc method uses topological image averaging.
source: This is done by using topological image averaging.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as part of the method description.

claim: The SiteLoc method is well suited for antibody binding site measurements on native cell surface morphology.
source: Our results show that this method is well suited for antibody binding site measurements on native cell surface morphology and that it can be applied to other molecular distance estimations as well.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the results.

claim: The SiteLoc method can be applied to other molecular distance estimations.
source: Our results show that this method is well suited for antibody binding site measurements on native cell surface morphology and that it can be applied to other molecular distance estimations as well.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the results.

claim: Antibody binding to pathogen surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity.
source: Antibody binding to pathogen surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity (Lu et al., 2018), and epitope localization affects diverse immunological outcomes, such as antibody neutralizing ability (Law et al., 2008; Kwong et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2019; Caoili, 2014; Ivanyi, 2014) or autoreactivity (Caoili, 2014; Cunningham, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2018.

claim: Epitope localization affects antibody neutralizing ability.
source: Antibody binding to pathogen surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity (Lu et al., 2018), and epitope localization affects diverse immunological outcomes, such as antibody neutralizing ability (Law et al., 2008; Kwong et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2019; Caoili, 2014; Ivanyi, 2014) or autoreactivity (Caoili, 2014; Cunningham, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Law et al., 2008; Kwong et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2019; Caoili, 2014; Ivanyi, 2014.

claim: Epitope localization affects autoreactivity.
source: Antibody binding to pathogen surface proteins plays a crucial role in immunity (Lu et al., 2018), and epitope localization affects diverse immunological outcomes, such as antibody neutralizing ability (Law et al., 2008; Kwong et al., 2013; Salinas et al., 2019; Caoili, 2014; Ivanyi, 2014) or autoreactivity (Caoili, 2014; Cunningham, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caoili, 2014; Cunningham, 2014.

claim: There are very few monoclonal antibodies clinically available for the treatment of bacterial infections.
source: Even though monoclonal antibody (mAb) treatments have proven to be successful for a wide spectrum of diseases, there are very few monoclonal antibodies clinically available for the treatment of bacterial infections (Motley et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Motley et al., 2019.

claim: Developing therapeutic mAbs against infections may require large-scale screening of highly conserved and functional epitopes.
source: Developing therapeutic mAbs against infections may require large-scale screening of highly conserved and functional epitopes (Martín-Galiano and McConnell, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Martín-Galiano and McConnell, 2019.

claim: Antibody epitopes are typically identified using crystallography, mutagenesis, or crosslinking coupled mass spectrometry.
source: Antibody epitopes are typically identified using crystallography, mutagenesis, or crosslinking coupled mass spectrometry (Abbott et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abbott et al., 2014.

claim: Current epitope identification methods are costly, time-consuming, and unsuitable for high-throughput analysis.
source: As of today, these methods are costly, time-consuming, and unsuitable for high-throughput analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of current methods mentioned in the introduction.

claim: Averaging methods for nanometer-scale localization on microscopy data exist but do not work for binding sites on proteins with heterogeneous expression on the cellular surface.
source: While averaging methods for nanometer-scale localization on microscopy data exist, these do not work for binding sites on proteins with heterogeneous expression on the cellular surface.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods.

claim: Existing averaging methods are designed for identical or spherical particles.
source: Moreover, they are designed for identical (Szymborska et al., 2013; Laine et al., 2015) or spherical (Son et al., 2020) particles and are thereby not fitted for unaltered cells due to the existing biological variation of surface morphology.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Szymborska et al., 2013; Laine et al., 2015; Son et al., 2020.

claim: Existing averaging methods are not fitted for unaltered cells due to biological variation of surface morphology.
source: Moreover, they are designed for identical (Szymborska et al., 2013; Laine et al., 2015) or spherical (Son et al., 2020) particles and are thereby not fitted for unaltered cells due to the existing biological variation of surface morphology.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods based on the nature of biological cells.

claim: The authors analyzed simulated images to assess the performance of the SiteLoc method.
source: To assess the performance of this method, we analyse simulated images, demonstrating high accuracy for varying surface expression and morphology.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as part of the validation approach.

claim: The SiteLoc method demonstrates high accuracy for varying surface expression and morphology in simulated images.
source: To assess the performance of this method, we analyse simulated images, demonstrating high accuracy for varying surface expression and morphology.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the simulated image analysis.

claim: The authors measured the height of DNA probes on erythrocyte surfaces to validate the method.
source: By measuring the height of DNA probes on erythrocyte surfaces, we show that our method can accurately estimate molecular heights on spherical and non-spherical cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as part of the validation approach.

claim: The SiteLoc method can accurately estimate molecular heights on spherical and non-spherical cells.
source: By measuring the height of DNA probes on erythrocyte surfaces, we show that our method can accurately estimate molecular heights on spherical and non-spherical cells.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the DNA probe measurements.

claim: The presented results with structured illumination microscopy (SIM) data achieve an ~10 nm precision certainty.
source: Our presented results with structured illumination microscopy (SIM) data achieve an ~10 nm precision certainty.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the SIM data analysis.

claim: The authors applied the site localization method to determine known binding site locales on M protein that is unevenly expressed on the bacterial surface of Streptococcus pyogenes.
source: We apply the site localization method to determine known binding site locales on M protein that is unevenly expressed on the bacterial surface of Streptococcus pyogenes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an application of the method.

claim: The SiteLoc method yields viable results when performed on widefield images with and without deconvolution.
source: Additionally, our method yields viable results when we perform site localization on widefield images with and without deconvolution.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the widefield image analysis.

claim: The site localization method enables rapid determination of binding sites without the need for synthetic modification of cell surface morphology.
source: To sum up, our site localization method enables rapid determination of binding sites without the need for synthetic modification of cell surface morphology.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a summary of the method's advantages.

claim: Binding site localization is based on resolving the axial distance between bound ligands and a reference surface.
source: Binding site localization is based on resolving the axial distance between bound ligands and a reference surface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a description of the method's principle.

claim: Nanometer-scale precision is achieved by dimension reduction of surface data within an image plane.
source: With this method, nanometer-scale precision is achieved by dimension reduction of surface data within an image plane.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a description of how the method achieves high precision.

claim: Fluorescently conjugated wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) binds bacterial peptidoglycan.
source: Fluorescently conjugated wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) that binds bacterial peptidoglycan is used here for the reference region, and antibodies that bind to bacterial M protein are labelled with another fluorescent dye for imaging in a separate channel (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated as a known property of WGA used in the method.

claim: M protein is unevenly distributed on bacterial surfaces.
source: The example shows how our method handles the uneven distribution of M protein on bacterial surfaces (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the example shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The SiteLoc method handles uneven distribution of M protein on bacterial surfaces.
source: The example shows how our method handles the uneven distribution of M protein on bacterial surfaces (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the method demonstrated in Figure 1b.

claim: Signal precision is improved as the distortion of an ovoid bacterium is accounted for through axial normalization in polar coordinates.
source: It is evident that the signal precision is improved as the distortion of an ovoid bacterium is accounted for through axial normalization in polar coordinates (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from Figure 1c showing improved signal-to-noise ratio.

claim: The perpendicular distance between the reference channel distribution and the target channel distribution in simulated images was chosen to be 2 px corresponding to 41 nm.
source: The perpendicular distance between the reference channel distribution and the target channel distribution was chosen to be 2 px corresponding to 41 nm using the pixel length of our N-SIM microscopy setup.
evidence: This is stated as a parameter of the simulation.

claim: For each chosen shape in the simulations, 100 time series were created with 10 frames each.
source: In order to mimic the experimental process of acquiring repeated frames of each data point in a time series, for each chosen shape 100 time series were created with 10 frames each.
evidence: This is stated as a parameter of the simulation.

claim: The SiteLoc method achieves high accuracy for various cell surface patterns in simulated images.
source: The results, shown in Figure 2, indicate that a high accuracy can be achieved for various cell surface patterns.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the simulated image analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: For certain shapes, the SiteLoc method yields a slightly larger distance than the true value.
source: However, for certain shapes, the method yields a slightly larger distance than the true value (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from Figure 2b.

claim: The uncertainty in site localization measurements is larger with secondary antibody labelling than with direct labelling.
source: As expected, the uncertainty is larger with secondary antibody labelling than with direct labelling.
evidence: This is stated as a result from additional simulations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The site localization uncertainty increases when the SNR is decreased.
source: The site localization uncertainty also increases when the SNR is decreased.
evidence: This is stated as a result from additional simulations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The results from simulated images demonstrate the robustness of the site localization method for varying surface expression and morphology.
source: These results demonstrate the robustness of the site localization method for varying surface expression and morphology.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the simulation results.

claim: Human erythrocytes were stained with membrane dye CellBrite Fix 488 and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated dsDNA of varying length.
source: Human erythrocytes were stained with membrane dye CellBrite Fix 488 and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated dsDNA of varying length (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Site localization measurements on swelled spherical erythrocytes show good agreement with an existing method for determining molecular heights on spherical particles.
source: To begin with, swelled spherical erythrocytes were analysed with the site localization method as well as with an existing method for determining molecular heights on spherical particles (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The results show good agreement.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Site localization performed on non-spherical erythrocytes shows results equivalent to that of spherical cells.
source: Site localization was thereafter performed on non-spherical erythrocytes and show results equivalent to that of spherical cells (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparison shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The measured heights of DNA probes are approximately half of the full length of the DNA strands.
source: The measured heights are approximately half of the full length of the DNA strands.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the DNA probe measurements.

claim: The measurements of DNA probe heights agree well with the predicted worm-like chain (WLC) model height for DNA strands with a persistence length of 50 nm.
source: The measurements agree well with the predicted worm-like chain (WLC) model height for DNA strands, with a persistence length of 50 nm (Baumann et al., 1997), tethered to a surface and able to freely rotate.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the DNA probe measurements, with citation to Baumann et al., 1997 for the persistence length.

claim: The SiteLoc method can accurately estimate molecular heights on spherical and non-spherical cellular surfaces.
source: Altogether, we show that our method can accurately estimate molecular heights on spherical and non-spherical cellular surfaces.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the DNA probe measurements.

claim: The antibody Fc binding site on M protein is located at the S region.
source: The antibody Fc binding site on M protein is located at the S region (Akesson et al., 1994), and a non-specific monoclonal IgG antibody (Xolair) is used for site localization of this binding.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Akesson et al., 1994.

claim: Ab49 is an M protein-specific mAb with an epitope located in the B3-S region.
source: Additionally, a measurement is carried out for an M protein-specific mAb, Ab49 (Bahnan et al., 2021), with an epitope located in the B3-S region, that is, slightly further along the IgGFc binding region.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bahnan et al., 2021.

claim: Fibrinogen has two binding sites on M protein at the B1 and B2 region.
source: For determining binding to the far end of M protein, we used fibrinogen that has two binding sites at the B1 and B2 region (Hauri et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hauri et al., 2019.

claim: The median resolved distance for the Xolair Fc binding site is 5.6 (29.7) nm.
source: The median resolved distance is [median (IQR)] 5.6 (29.7) nm for the Xolair Fc binding site, 6.2 (29.8) nm for Ab49 Fab binding site, and 18.0 (49.3) nm for the two fibrinogen binding sites.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the site localization measurements on S. pyogenes.

claim: The median resolved distance for the Ab49 Fab binding site is 6.2 (29.8) nm.
source: The median resolved distance is [median (IQR)] 5.6 (29.7) nm for the Xolair Fc binding site, 6.2 (29.8) nm for Ab49 Fab binding site, and 18.0 (49.3) nm for the two fibrinogen binding sites.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the site localization measurements on S. pyogenes.

claim: The median resolved distance for the two fibrinogen binding sites is 18.0 (49.3) nm.
source: The median resolved distance is [median (IQR)] 5.6 (29.7) nm for the Xolair Fc binding site, 6.2 (29.8) nm for Ab49 Fab binding site, and 18.0 (49.3) nm for the two fibrinogen binding sites.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the site localization measurements on S. pyogenes.

claim: The presented results for antibody and fibrinogen binding sites on M protein are consistent with the arrangement of the binding sites as reported in the literature.
source: The presented results are consistent with the arrangement of the binding sites as reported in the literature (Akesson et al., 1994; Bahnan et al., 2021; Hauri et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the binding site measurements, with citations to previous literature.

claim: Site localization precision is increased when using directly conjugated antibodies compared to secondary antibody labelling.
source: It is evident from these results that site localization precision is increased when using directly conjugated antibodies.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The SiteLoc method can yield viable results with widefield images.
source: By performing site localization measurements on widefield images, we show that our method can yield viable results even with conventional microscopy data.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the widefield image analysis.

claim: Deconvolution of widefield images may yield an increase in precision for site localization measurements.
source: Moreover, deconvolution of the widefield images may yield an increase in precision.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparison of widefield and deconvolved widefield images.

claim: For fibrinogen samples, the median resolved distance is 18.0 (49.3) nm with SIM data, 38.5 (71.0) nm with widefield data, and 40.1 (42.0) nm with deconvolved widefield data.
source: For the fibrinogen samples (Figure 5b), the median resolved distance between the two channels is [median (IQR)] 18.0 (49.3) nm with SIM data, 38.5 (71.0) nm with widefield data, and 40.1 (42.0) nm with deconvolved widefield data.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparison of different imaging modalities shown in Figure 5b.

claim: For Xolair samples, the median resolved distance is 5.6 (29.7) nm with SIM data, 12.3 (76.5) nm with widefield data, and 14.2 (34.5) nm with deconvolved widefield data.
source: For the Xolair samples (Figure 5d), the median resolved distance for the Xolair Fc binding site is 5.6 (29.7) nm with SIM data, 12.3 (76.5) nm with widefield data, and 14.2 (34.5) nm with deconvolved widefield data.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparison of different imaging modalities shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The site localization method performs well with widefield images.
source: This indicates that the site localization method performs well with widefield images and that the precision can be increased through deconvolution.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the widefield image analysis.

claim: The precision of site localization can be increased through deconvolution of widefield images.
source: This indicates that the site localization method performs well with widefield images and that the precision can be increased through deconvolution.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the comparison of widefield and deconvolved widefield images.

claim: The locations of protein binding sites on cellular surfaces are important for a wide range of cellular processes.
source: The locations of protein binding sites on cellular surfaces are important for a wide range of cellular processes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: How and where an antibody binds to pathogen surface structures is critical for the outcome of host-pathogen interactions.
source: In particular, how and where an antibody binds to pathogen surface structures is critical for the outcome of host-pathogen interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: Bacteria are known to target antibodies in many different ways.
source: This is especially relevant for bacteria as they are known to target antibodies in many different ways (Nordenfelt et al., 2012; Nordenfelt and Björck, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nordenfelt et al., 2012; Nordenfelt and Björck, 2013.

claim: Knowing the location of the epitope greatly aids both mechanistic understanding and facilitates potential therapeutic development.
source: Knowing the location of the epitope greatly aids both mechanistic understanding and facilitates potential therapeutic development.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion about the importance of epitope localization.

claim: Super-resolution techniques such as iPALM, STORM, and STED can in practice achieve an ~10 nm resolution.
source: Super-resolution techniques such as iPALM, STORM, and STED can in practice achieve an ~10 nm resolution but are costly imaging systems that typically require complex sample preparation.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of existing super-resolution techniques.

claim: Super-resolution techniques such as iPALM, STORM, and STED are costly imaging systems that typically require complex sample preparation.
source: Super-resolution techniques such as iPALM, STORM, and STED can in practice achieve an ~10 nm resolution but are costly imaging systems that typically require complex sample preparation.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of existing super-resolution techniques.

claim: An ~10 nm (~12 nm IQR, ~9 nm SD) precision is achieved with diffraction-limited microscopy images by dimension reduction of surface data within an image plane.
source: Here, an ~10 nm (~12 nm IQR, ~9 nm SD) precision is achieved with diffraction-limited microscopy images by dimension reduction of surface data within an image plane.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the method's performance.

claim: Existing imaging-based averaging methods are designed for identical or spherical particles and therefore not suited for site localization on native cell surface morphology.
source: Existing imaging-based averaging methods are designed for identical or spherical particles and therefore not suited for site localization on native cell surface morphology.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods.

claim: The SiteLoc method enables site localization on native cell surface morphology through normalization of the axial positions of a reference surface.
source: This is made possible with our method through normalization of the axial positions of a reference surface.
evidence: This is stated as a key feature of the method that distinguishes it from existing methods.

claim: A 1 nm precision could be achievable under ideal conditions with the SiteLoc method.
source: These results indicate that a 1 nm precision could be achievable under ideal conditions and show that the site localization method is highly accurate for varying topologies and inhomogeneous surface expression.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the simulation results.

claim: The site localization method is highly accurate for varying topologies and inhomogeneous surface expression.
source: These results indicate that a 1 nm precision could be achievable under ideal conditions and show that the site localization method is highly accurate for varying topologies and inhomogeneous surface expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the simulation results.

claim: The SiteLoc method is suited for cells with non-spherical topology.
source: Our presented results show that this method is suited even for cells with non-spherical topology.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the results on bacterial M protein.

claim: It has proven difficult to perform site localization measurements on bacteria.
source: However, it has proven difficult to perform site localization measurements on bacteria.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental work.

claim: The difficulty in performing site localization measurements on bacteria may be due to the small size of bacteria.
source: This may be due to the small size of bacteria.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the source of difficulty.

claim: The variation in site localization measurements can be minimized by increasing SNR.
source: Furthermore, our in silico experiments, as well as our in vitro experiments, indicate that the variation in the measurements can be minimized by increasing SNR and minimizing the biological variability, for example, by using directly conjugated antibodies instead of secondary labelling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the in silico and in vitro experiments.

claim: The variation in site localization measurements can be minimized by using directly conjugated antibodies instead of secondary labelling.
source: Furthermore, our in silico experiments, as well as our in vitro experiments, indicate that the variation in the measurements can be minimized by increasing SNR and minimizing the biological variability, for example, by using directly conjugated antibodies instead of secondary labelling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the in silico and in vitro experiments.

claim: The SiteLoc method may be useful for rapid screening of epitope locales.
source: We believe this method may be useful for rapid screening of epitope locales, and the implementation, written in the open-source language Julia, is provided on GitHub.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the method.

claim: The implementation of the SiteLoc method is written in the open-source language Julia and is provided on GitHub.
source: We believe this method may be useful for rapid screening of epitope locales, and the implementation, written in the open-source language Julia, is provided on GitHub.
evidence: This is stated as information about the availability of the method.

claim: S. pyogenes strain SF370 expresses M1 protein on its surface.
source: Strain SF370 expresses M1 protein on its surface and is available through the American Type Culture Collection (ATCC 700294) (Ferretti et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ferretti et al., 2001.

claim: Xolair (omalizumab) is a humanized monoclonal IgG that is IgE-specific.
source: Xolair (omalizumab, Novartis) is a humanized monoclonal IgG that is IgE-specific, and thus only binds to M protein via Fc.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the antibody used in the experiments.

claim: Xolair only binds to M protein via Fc.
source: Xolair (omalizumab, Novartis) is a humanized monoclonal IgG that is IgE-specific, and thus only binds to M protein via Fc.
evidence: This is stated as a property of Xolair relevant to the experiments.

claim: IdeS is an enzyme that cleaves IgG at the hinge region, separating the F(ab')2 from the Fc.
source: For secondary antibody labelling, both antibodies were treated with IdeS (Hansa Biopharma) (von Pawel-Rammingen et al., 2002), an enzyme that cleaves IgG at the hinge region, separating the F(ab')2 from the Fc.
evidence: This is supported by citation to von Pawel-Rammingen et al., 2002.

claim: The widefield images were deconvolved using the Richardson–Lucy algorithm in 10 iterations.
source: The widefield images were deconvolved using the Richardson–Lucy algorithm (Richardson, 1972; Lucy, 1974) in 10 iterations.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the image processing method, with citations to Richardson, 1972; Lucy, 1974.

claim: The measured offset in dual-labeled cell wall experiments is likely due to chromatic aberration at the imaging plane.
source: The measured offset, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, is likely due to chromatic aberration at the imaging plane.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the offset measurements.

claim: The offset from dual-labeled cell wall experiments is used to correct for chromatic aberration in subsequent site localization measurements.
source: This offset is used to correct for chromatic aberration in subsequent site localization measurements by correcting the position of the reference region prior to calculating distance to the ligand signal.
evidence: This is stated as a description of how the offset is used in the analysis.
